rules.name: speed is structure, not arithmetic
rules.note: Every large factor measured in this repo came from noticing the system HAD A PROPERTY and then not doing the work that property made unnecessary -- not from faster arithmetic, and not from a network that predicts forces. This is a claim about where to look. It cannot be unit-tested, and saying so is more honest than inventing a check that would pass either way.

rules.name: every test must be able to fail
rules.note: 7 probes audited; controls (declared, unfalsifiable by construction): ['linearity -> superposition']; discriminators all seen failing somewhere

rules.name: a threshold must be anchored to something invariant
rules.note: n_null 6 unchanged when the operator is multiplied by 1e12 (gap 1.45e+13 -> 1.45e+13)

rules.name: "could not tell" is not "none"
rules.note: grounded operator: noise 4.8e-02 relative, calibration declined, verdict NOT TESTABLE

rules.name: graded, not binary
rules.note: 1.5x from the threshold -> MARGINAL; 1e6x over -> FAILS; 1e-6x under -> HOLDS

rules.name: two independent computations, or you will not notice
rules.note: setup 6 @ gap 1.45e+13; independent k=64 solve 6 @ gap 1.45e+13

rules.name: a probe must confirm it perturbed something
rules.note: check itself raised AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'solve'

rules.name: the negative is the deliverable
rules.note: a FAILS record carries the same fields as a HOLDS record

rules.name: predeclare
rules.note: The gates go in the docstring before the run, so that a surprising number cannot be reinterpreted after the fact into a result. Nothing mechanical can verify this -- the check would be whether I wrote the gate before or after seeing the number, and only the commit history knows that. Claimed, not proven, and marked as such.

log: THE DOCTRINE -- the rules, and a check for each that can fail
Every rule below is the generalisation of a specific defect that produced a specific wrong
number in this repo. Stated principles are free, so each one that can be checked is checked
against the toolchain as it stands -- and each check is then run against a deliberate
reintroduction of the original defect, because a check that cannot fail is not a check.
corpus: 700 points, three operators (plain, rescaled 1e12, grounded)
DECLARED CONTROLS -- exempt from rule 2, and never counted as a reduction
linearity -> superposition
cannot fail on a linear solver -- every Hessian is linear, so this verifies the operator and
the solve rather than a property of the system. A FAILS here means the Hessian is wrong and
nothing else in the run means anything. It is the reason probe_finite_linearity exists.
